Experiment: Plain Gaussian Monte Carlo

Experiment: Antithetic + exact-radius sphere + anchored layer-1 control variate
Result: Best combined adjusted score 4.91e-7; component gains: antithetic 1.09x, sphere 1.04x, anchored CV 1.24–1.71x; best total 1.56x.

Experiment: Two independently scrambled Sobol sphere streams with antipodal pairing and exact radius
Result: Adjusted 3.4607e-7 vs previous 4.91e-7 (29.5% lower); frozen IDs 50–99: 3.6309e-7; 0 failures.

Experiment: 66,048-point Kerdock/MUB spherical 5-design with FWHT first layer
Result: Raw MSE 2.2826e-7; adjusted 2.2566e-7 vs Sobol 3.4607e-7; 34.8% adjusted improvement; frozen holdout improved 25.0%.

Experiment: Energy-weighted K3 carrier sketch
Result: K3-simple error 4.4663e-5 → 2.4724e-5 (44.6% lower), 9/10 MLPs improved, estimated 3.27% budget; not competitive standalone.

Experiment: Cheap per-network statistics used to choose Kerdock/Sobol rotations

Experiment: 90,624-row two-rotation pilot
Result: Raw-MSE gains varied by evaluation split (roughly 10–23%), but the rule uses 90,624 rather than 66,048 rows (+37.2%). The exact depth-32 kernel predicts only about 10.45% MSE reduction, implying an error-cost ratio near 1.229.
Verdict: Genuine raw-accuracy gain, but honestly accounted adjusted score is worse; closed.
Primary source: Multifidelity audit and latest multi-agent update, 2026-07-28

Experiment: Cheaper 78,336-row rotated pilot
Result: Predicted error-cost ratio 1.091x relative to baseline.
Verdict: Rejected

Experiment: Best single added rotated basis
Result: Predicted error-cost ratio 1.0012x.

Experiment: Fixed-count basis swaps at 66,048 rows
Result: Best result 1.0029x MSE relative to baseline.

Experiment: Random orthonormal basis + antipodes

Experiment: One Kerdock basis

Experiment: Eight pairwise-MUB bases under a common rotation
Result: Effective variance 0.0198 vs Haar 0.0298 vs Sobol 0.0418; about 2.1x better than Sobol in that test.

Experiment: IID, Sobol, orthogonal, and generic antipodal pilots
Result: Orthogonal/IID next-sigma ratio 1.006 with wide interval [0.92,1.09]; mean MSE favored orthogonal over IID by ~1.70x [1.02,2.71]; generic antipodal helped means but hurt covariance.

Experiment: 4,096-point IID, Sobol, orthogonal pilots
Result: Next-sigma errors: IID 1.53%, Sobol 1.44%, orthogonal 1.49%; mean sampling constant improved about 25–40%.

Experiment: Interlaced order-2 Sobol

Experiment: Random two-dimensional plane angular integration

Experiment: Nested Richardson extrapolation

Experiment: Exact Gaussian-line propagation

Experiment: Smoothed-delta forward-Laplacian proxy

Experiment: Same-cost mixtures and doubled-compute blends of sampling designs
Result: Best same-cost mixture gained about 1.09x; doubled-compute optimal blend gained 1.66x MSE, below the 2x needed to offset cost.
Verdict: Closed / score-negative

Experiment: Jacobian/eigenvector-derived point sets
Result: Concentrated samples into too few activation regions and performed hundreds to thousands of times worse in tested cases.

Experiment: Powered one-step comparison of IID, Sobol antipodal, signed-Hadamard bases, and Haar-orthogonal antipodal bases
Result: Next-layer sigma RMS: IID 1.4201%, Sobol 1.3609%, signed-Hadamard 1.3790%, Haar 1.3352%. IID/Haar ratio 1.0636; paired 95% CI [1.0220, 1.1093].

Experiment: Combined Haar-versus-Sobol comparison for sigma and final means
Result: Final direct and recursive Edgeworth means were statistically tied. Haar sigma RMS 1.3726% versus Sobol 1.4195%; Sobol/Haar ratio 1.0342, 95% CI [1.0153, 1.0547].

Experiment: Sigma RMS at 512, 1,024, 2,048, and 4,096 points
Verdict: Consistent variance-constant reduction

Experiment: Recursive fourth-order Edgeworth final MSE under IID, Haar, and Sobol pilots
Result: IID/Haar MSE ratios: 1.58, 1.65, 1.82, and 1.62 at 512, 1,024, 2,048, and 4,096 points; every paired interval excluded no improvement. High-count absolute differences were truth-noise limited.

Experiment: Haar pilots at 4,096, 5,120, 6,144, and 6,656 points
Result: Sigma RMS improved 1.226% -> 1.135% -> 1.066% -> 1.044%; observed Edgeworth MSE approached the 6.70e-6 reference-noise floor.

Experiment: Full Sobol, full Haar, 50/50 and 25/75 mixtures, and split Sobol scrambles

Experiment: Select a lucky fixed 6,144-point Haar seed
Result: A discovery-suite 40% advantage disappeared on new networks; fresh/fixed Edgeworth ratio 1.110 with 95% CI [0.812, 1.418], and fixed sigma was slightly worse.

Experiment: Random signed-Hadamard sign/permutation search for Kerdock-like geometry
Result: Fourth frame potential stayed near 3 rather than the MUB value 1; random search barely changed it.
Verdict: Not a route to Kerdock geometry

Experiment: One-, three-, and five-factor randomized Hadamard products versus dense Haar QR
Result: Sigma RMS: Haar 1.3536%; one factor 1.3826%; three factors 1.3947%; five factors 1.3952%. Similar low-order frame potentials did not recover Haar performance.

Experiment: Spherical Stein directional control variate
Result: 2.10x worse than baseline.
Verdict: Failed

Experiment: Degree-2 spherical harmonic control, theoretical coefficient

Result: 0.98x; statistically indistinguishable.

Experiment: Quadratic controls, rank 16 and rank 32

Experiment: Cross-fitted layer-1 linear control
Result: Raw MSE ratio 0.93x, but cost about 3% of budget; net score wash.

Experiment: Degree-1, degree-2, and degree-4 Hermite control variates

Experiment: Naive recursive linear mean control variate
Result: Collapses algebraically back to the sample mean.
Verdict: No independent benefit

Experiment: Exact layer 1 before recursive control variate
Verdict: Small gain

Experiment: Conditional-Hermite structural closure
Result: About 1.68x gain.
Verdict: Modest positive

Experiment: Radial covariance deconvolution
Result: About 1.06x gain.
Verdict: Tiny positive

Experiment: Affine-tail multilevel Monte Carlo
Result: First two networks predicted 1.9–3.5x efficiency; direct validation after training gave 1.26x vs ~2.7x predicted.
Verdict: Small real gain, model overoptimistic

Experiment: Linear surrogate g = diag(Phi(mu/sigma))(z-mu) with true surrogate variance
Result: 6,000-sample sigma error fell from 2.07% to 0.65%; late layers reached roughly 0.42–0.45%.
Verdict: Real oracle variance-reduction mechanism

Experiment: Same local surrogate with analytically approximated surrogate variance
Result: The surrogate variance was wrong by about 7%; reported error worsened from roughly 2.33% to 6.82%.
Verdict: Failed because anchor expectation is inaccurate

Experiment: Estimate surrogate variance using an independent orthogonal or Kerdock stream
Result: Reduced error only 13–16% while approximately doubling compute.
Verdict: Score-negative

Experiment: Recursive residual correction using Gaussian, Sobol, orthogonal, or Kerdock-subset directions
Result: At width 64 structured directions helped strongly; at width 256 results were Gaussian 3.95e-6, Sobol 2.33e-6, orthogonal 4.42e-6, Kerdock subset 3.63e-6.
Verdict: Some direct-QMC gain, not a competitive recursive correction

Experiment: Reduce recursive covariance correction from 6,000 rows to 128 rows
Result: Predictions changed negligibly; estimated total compute fraction was about 10.4%.
Verdict: Useful implementation fact, insufficient accuracy

Experiment: Affine Gaussian-sample recursive CV with 128-row covariance sketch
Result: Final mean MSE 6.92e-6 -> 4.06e-6 (1.71x); 90% of networks improved; projected adjusted proxy 4.2e-7. Separate held-out blend gain was only about 1.22x.
Verdict: Legitimate improvement but worse than Kerdock

Experiment: Apply homogeneous recursive correction to full antipodal Kerdock design
Result: Recursive and direct Kerdock predictions agreed to approximately 1e-12 because the homogeneous recursion telescopes.
Verdict: Exact no-op; branch closed

Experiment: Exact degree-1 Hermite controls across layers
Result: Helped early layers slightly but lost usefulness with depth.
Verdict: Not a full-depth solution

Experiment: Blend direct radial pilot means with Edgeworth predictions from the same pilot at 512–4,096 points
Result: Best scalar blends improved MSE by only about 0.01–0.14%; all paired intervals included no improvement.
Verdict: Closed; errors too redundant

Experiment: Direct Haar radial mean, fourth-order Edgeworth, tuned blend, and equal average
Result: Held-out MSE: direct 6.93e-6; Edgeworth 7.70e-6; tuned blend 7.00e-6; average 7.13e-6. Direct/blend ratio 0.990, 95% CI [0.955, 1.025].
Verdict: Direct/Edgeworth blend rejected

Experiment: Full Gaussian mean/covariance propagation
Result: Final MSE 6.19e-5, roughly 270x worse than strong sampling.
Verdict: Failed baseline

Experiment: Gaussian marginals with exact per-layer mean and covariance
Result: MSE 1.25e-6, around Monte Carlo parity.
Verdict: Shows Gaussian marginal ceiling

Experiment: Edgeworth with κ3
Result: MSE 1.86e-7 vs Gaussian 1.25e-6.
Verdict: Strong improvement

Experiment: Edgeworth with κ3 and κ4
Result: MSE 3.84e-8, about 32x better than Gaussian oracle.
Verdict: Best oracle marginal model

Experiment: Edgeworth extended through κ5 and κ6
Result: MSE worsened to 4.37e-8.
Verdict: Higher order did not help

Experiment: Propagate mean; sample sigma and cumulants
Result: Measured MSE ~6.0e-6 vs 9.6e-6 predicted.
Verdict: Failed to beat sampling

Experiment: Replace propagated sigma with sampled sigma at 6k/25k/67k/400k samples
Result: Sigma error 1.83%/0.89%/0.55%/0.22%; MSE 3.62e-6/1.10e-6/2.81e-7/1.48e-7. Best in-budget adjusted score still worse than cubature.

Experiment: Independent sigma-error injection across layers
Result: Originally implied ~0.1% sigma accuracy; later shown too pessimistic because injected noise structure was unrealistic.

Experiment: Exact covariance at six worst layers, 19 deep layers, or all layers
Result: MSE: none 2.82e-5; six layers 9.23e-6; 19 layers 5.28e-6; all 32 layers 2.82e-7.
Verdict: Local patches fail; errors reappear

Experiment: Supply exact means alone or exact means and sigmas from layers 5/25/31
Result: From layer 25: mean only 1.29e-5 vs mean+sigma 3.08e-7; about 42x gap attributable to sigma over last eight layers.
Verdict: Sigma was dominant in this architecture

Experiment: Exact sigma only for neurons with |μ/σ| below thresholds
Verdict: Need most neurons recursively

Experiment: Per-layer and per-(layer, |t|) calibration
Result: Per-(layer,|t|) held-out ratio 0.96x; earlier per-layer version much worse. No useful gain in tested calibration families.
Verdict: Failed tested calibrations

Experiment: Activation covariance effective-rank collapse
Result: Effective rank fell from about 160–165 to 2.7–3 by depth 32.
Verdict: Important structural diagnostic

Experiment: Low-rank approximation of third cumulant
Result: At layers 26/30, covariance rank ~3 but κ3 needed rank around 64 for small error; r=8 errors ~0.29, r=64 ~0.03–0.05.
Verdict: Killed naive low-rank κ3 route

Experiment: Rank truncation of activation batch
Result: Rank 8 over only last four layers produced about 600x the noise target.
Verdict: Failed catastrophically

Experiment: Fit a Gaussian at layer k, sample from it, then propagate exactly
Result: About 5e-6 for every handoff layer k=2…28.
Verdict: Failed; distortions amplified

Experiment: Teacher-forced learned closures vs free rollout
Result: Free rollout was 16–21x worse than teacher-forced.
Verdict: Failed due state/rollout mismatch

Experiment: Correct covariance diagonal only
Result: Sigma error 3.70% → 3.64%.
Verdict: Failed; error mostly off-diagonal

Experiment: Shrink dominant covariance eigenvalue by 7.5–10%
Result: Reduced Gaussian-closure MSE roughly 2.3–2.5x across 32 networks.
Verdict: Repeatable but far from competitive

Experiment: Blend sampled moments/covariance with Gaussian closure
Result: Did not beat direct sampling at equal sample count; another experiment improved 9.80% → 4.61% but remained worse than direct methods.
Verdict: Failed as a competitive hybrid

Experiment: Best rank-r approximation of covariance correction
Verdict: Residual is compressible in oracle form

Experiment: Estimate low-rank correction from 8,192 pilot samples
Result: Stayed around 2.2% error despite oracle rank-16 reaching 0.5%.
Verdict: Failed to identify subspace

Experiment: Measure switching after apparent gate stabilization
Result: Median |μ/σ| ~3.31, but about 12.8 sign deviations/input and sensitivity-weighted switching around 30%.
Verdict: Rare-switching expansion not justified

Experiment: Classify neurons always-on/off from 1,200-input pilot
Result: About 39% appeared stable, but some had true missed-switch probabilities ~0.4–0.46%.
Verdict: Exact pruning unsafe

Experiment: Globally scale positive weights to simplify gates
Result: Positive homogeneity leaves activation regions and standardized moments unchanged.
Verdict: Dead analytically

Experiment: Naive Gaussian mixture and Gaussian-copula models
Result: Neither beat directly estimating the target moment from the same pilot samples.
Verdict: Failed implementations

Experiment: Universal symmetric bivariate residual model with oracle current moments
Result: Held-out residual R² 0.85; residual RMSE improved 2.84x; one-step next-sigma 3.18% → 1.62%; width-256 check about 2x.

Experiment: Extended model with accurate current-layer moments
Verdict: Near target with oracle moments

Experiment: Same model using 900–1,200-sample pilot moments
Result: 900 samples: 3.69% vs direct empirical covariance 3.13%; width 256/1,200: 2.33% vs empirical 2.29%.

Experiment: Full recursive rollout
Result: Final sigma error 25.3% → 14.2%, but final mean MSE worsened 3.23e-4 → 1.11e-3.

Experiment: Edgeworth mean alone; learned covariance with Gaussian mean; both together
Result: Edgeworth mean alone: 3.23e-4 → 1.59e-4. Learned covariance + Gaussian mean: 2.57e-4. Full combination failed.

Experiment: Scale Edgeworth mean correction on top of learned covariance
Result: 25% roughly neutral; 50% already worse.
Verdict: Did not resolve inconsistency

Experiment: Increase pilot size and train residual denoiser
Result: Model fit R² ~0.98, but learned all-pairs covariance was worse than empirical at every sample size; at 4,800, empirical 2.17% vs learned 3.87%.

Experiment: Optimize correction for downstream sigma and shrink toward empirical covariance
Result: Optimal solution was effectively 100% empirical covariance.

Experiment: O(n²) closure using c21, c31, c22, correlation, skew, kurtosis
Result: Gaussian map 9.80%; accurate moments 1.48%; moments from 1,000 samples 2.41%; transfer retained ~3.0–3.7x improvement on deeper/wider networks.

Experiment: Per-neuron EMP residual regression on local features
Result: Train R² 0.177; held-out R² −0.118.

Family: Linear residual control variate for covariance

Result: Width 64/depth 32: Gaussian 4.32%; direct sample 8,192: 0.886%; CV 4,096: 0.441%; CV 8,192: 0.290%; cross-fit 0.304%; oracle regression 0.159%.

Experiment: Low-rank factors plus diagonal particle/covariance model
Result: Failed badly / poor reconstruction.

Experiment: Jacobian and actual error-impact spectra

Verdict: Higher moments are estimable but expensive

Result: Performance became roughly tied with directly sampled sigma at about 1.8–2.4%; the earlier ~0.9% result relied on oracle first/second moments.

Result: Improved early layers but worsened deep-layer errors by roughly 14–48%.

Result: Gaussian final MSE 8.52e-5; oracle strengths 0.25 and 0.50 gave 6.53e-5 and 3.92e-5; 0.75 was unstable; 6,000-sample correction was unstable even at low strengths.

Experiment: Raw sample covariance versus Ledoit–Wolf and OAS
Result: Quadratic-form errors 2.1096%, 2.1089%, and 2.1082%, respectively.
Verdict: No meaningful gain

Experiment: Replace/correct top sample-eigenvector blocks of size 8–128
Verdict: Relevant covariance defect remains high-dimensional

Experiment: Learn pair residuals with ordinary pairwise loss
Result: Held-out pair residual R2 about 0.91, but contracted next-variance error worsened to 4.68% versus 2.19% for direct sampled covariance.
Verdict: Pairwise RMSE/R2 is the wrong objective

Experiment: Naive empirical Mehler and Hermite expansions at increasing order
Result: Became unstable at moderate order and worsened deep-layer errors.
Verdict: Failed in naive form

Experiment: Term-wise shrinkage of noisy Edgeworth corrections
Result: Improved error by only about 4%.
Verdict: Too small

Experiment: Use structured directions for centered M21, M22, and M31 estimates
Result: Did not improve consistently; cancellation dominated the estimates.
Verdict: No reliable gain

Experiment: Fit a global quadratic/calibration direction on official records
Result: Gained 2.2% in-sample but worsened the untouched records; held-out gain about 0.996x.
Verdict: Does not generalize

Experiment: Universal extra-trees and histogram-gradient-boosting pair-residual models
Result: Extra-trees pair R2 0.561 and next-sigma RMS 1.782%; HGB R2 0.746 and 1.699%; direct empirical covariance achieved 1.459%.
Verdict: Residual is learnable, but model loses downstream

Experiment: Allow model to see empirical pilot ReLU residual features
Result: Pair residual R2 reached 0.904 and next-sigma RMS 1.467%, still slightly worse than direct empirical covariance at 1.459%.

Experiment: Blend empirical covariance with learned pair correction
Result: Chosen beta was 0.05 for universal models and 0.575 for pilot-aware model; best apparent gain was below 0.03% relative and within uncertainty.
Verdict: Closed for current models/features

Experiment: Combine learned covariance and Edgeworth mean corrections separately and jointly
Result: Learned covariance reduced final sigma error about 25.3% -> 14.2%; each component helped with the other Gaussian, but applying both at full strength worsened final mean MSE.
Verdict: Approximate mean and covariance states are mutually inconsistent

Experiment: Measure modal-sign deviations and sensitivity-weighted switching
Result: Sensitivity-weighted switching remained around 30%, despite large median |mu/sigma| in deep layers.
Verdict: Global rare-switch expansion closed

Experiment: Validate neurons labeled always-on/off by a finite pilot
Result: Some candidates had true switching probabilities around 0.4–0.46 under larger samples.
Verdict: Pilot-only exact pruning unsafe

Experiment: Scale every layer by positive global factors
Result: Activation regions and standardized moments are unchanged; activations only receive deterministic scale powers.
Verdict: Closed analytically

Experiment: Naive Gaussian-mixture and Gaussian-copula pair estimators
Result: Did not beat direct empirical pair moments at matched samples.
Verdict: Closed in tested forms

Experiment: Models trained on next-layer variance corrections and analytic/empirical covariance shrinkage
Result: Held-out models selected almost entirely empirical covariance and produced no material improvement.
Verdict: Closed for current feature/model classes

Experiment: Dense Kerdock propagation
Result: ~268.4B analytical FLOPs.
Verdict: Reference implementation

Experiment: Three-level batched Strassen
Result: ~211.1B analytical FLOPs; projected local adjusted score ~1.79e-7.

Experiment: Three-level Winograd variant
Result: ~208.0B projected; projected score ~1.75e-7.

Experiment: First Strassen submission
Result: Timed out / failed all MLPs because implementation overhead exceeded guard.

Experiment: Replace einsum with fnp.matmul and improve batching
Result: Matmul measured ~69x faster; local runtime 18.75s → 5.28s. Graded score 2.39e-7 because residual wall-clock erased projected benefit.

Experiment: Assembly-free / persistent-layout Kerdock-Winograd kernel
Result: 170.91B tracked, 175.52B effective, multiplier 0.6453, no failures; one-network adjusted result ~1.12e-7. Not validated over full official suite in supplied logs.

Experiment: Quadtree assembly-free transform
Result: Reduced billed work by ~2.8%; persistent layout retained.
Verdict: Small positive

Experiment: Five-coordinate rank-7 factorization
Result: Reduced additions but wall-clock/materialization overhead was worse.
Verdict: Rejected

Experiment: Alternative-basis Strassen construction
Result: Algebraically worked, but finite-size arithmetic cost was worse than Winograd.
Verdict: Rejected

Experiment: Drezner–Wesolowsky integral after r=sin(theta), 8-node quadrature
Result: Matched Cho–Saul arc-cosine kernel to ~1.1e-16.
Verdict: Successful numerical primitive

Evidence level: Analytical FLOP proxy; grader validation pending
Experiment: Complete Haar bases at 10, 11, 12, and 13 bases
Result: 5,120 points 7.880%; 5,632 8.668%; 6,144 9.456%; 6,656 10.244% of budget from sample-forward FLOPs alone. Excludes moment operations and residual wall time.
Verdict: Start with 5,632; validate actual accounting

Experiment: Compose infinite-width ReLU dual kernel and expand in Gegenbauer harmonics
Result: At d=256/depth32, ~39.8% of nonconstant variance above degree 12; heavy tail robust.
Verdict: Core theoretical model

Experiment: Closed-form harmonic potentials from Kerdock/MUB inner products
Result: Exact cancellation through degree 5; N·P6=2.062035; limiting-kernel MSE 2.43366e-7; gain 1.572x vs IID.
Verdict: Successful / central result

Experiment: Predict Kerdock-vs-Sobol gain from spectrum and point geometry
Result: Predicted 1.4972x; measured 1.4855x; 0.78% discrepancy. Absolute Kerdock prediction within ~5%.
Verdict: Strong validation

Experiment: Monomial-to-Gegenbauer recurrence and truncation convergence
Result: Harmonic reconstruction at truncation 4,096 agreed with direct kernel evaluation to 0.071%; avoided negative-variance cancellation.
Verdict: Successful

Experiment: Optimize weights over the 129 Kerdock bases and competing configurations
Result: Uniform Kerdock/MUB weights remained optimal for fixed support/family; unequal basis weighting did not help.
Verdict: Closed within tested family

Experiment: d=4 MUB perturbations and random searches
Result: 224,000 tangent perturbations, 4,000 random configurations, and 6,000 orthogonal-basis searches initially found nothing better; closest alternatives ≥11% worse.
Verdict: Strong local evidence, later superseded globally

Experiment: d=16, N=288 comparison
Result: Median limiting-kernel MSE: MUB 5.3e-5; random orthogonal 6.4e-5; Sobol 7.1e-5; IID antipodal 8.2e-5; optimized random orthogonal still 21.7% worse.
Verdict: Strong evidence for MUB

Experiment: First-order finite-width correction and direct finite-network tests
Result: Correction helped shallow networks but sometimes failed badly at depth; finite-width effects were nonuniform.
Verdict: Infinite-width model not exact at width 256

Experiment: Delsarte-style auxiliary polynomial at d=256/depth32/N=66,048
Result: Kerdock 2.433660e-7 vs numerical lower bound 2.428983e-7: within ~0.192% of optimal among nonnegative-weight rules. Lacks interval-certified continuum proof. This first bound was later tightened to a 0.02337% maximum gap.
Verdict: Superseded by T13 tightened certificate

Experiment: Explicit d=4, 24-point configurations optimized against deep-ReLU kernel
Result: Relative to MUB: 0.96353 at depth4, 0.99873 at depth16, 0.99983 at depth32; finite-width confirmation at widths 64/256 with paired z≈−5.0/−9.7.
Verdict: Disproves exact global optimality from design exactness

Experiment: Complete Riemannian Hessian at d=4 MUB
Result: Depths 1–64: exactly six rotational zero modes and all other eigenvalues positive; depth32 smallest nonrotational eigenvalue 1.96e-5.
Verdict: Strict antipodal local minimum

Experiment: Coupled finite-width simulation, common randomness, Sobol QMC innovations, first-order 1/width corrections
Result: Target difference remained too noisy; first-order correction unreliable at large depth.
Verdict: Open / inconclusive

Experiment: KKT-tightened degree-5 Delsarte auxiliary polynomial at d=256, depth32, N=66,048
Result: Final V5 package certifies 1 <= Kerdock/optimum <= 1.0002336550102949. Relative excess is therefore in [0, 0.02336550102949%] for the stated infinite-width, network-independent, nonnegative-weight estimator class.
Verdict: Theorem complete within explicit scope; static positive-weight cubature is effectively closed.
Primary source: V5 proof package and clean-room audit, 2026-07-28

Experiment: Apply tightened auxiliary bound at d=4, d=16, and d=256
Result: Maximum possible improvements over MUB: 0.8757%, 0.2764%, and 0.02337%, respectively.
Verdict: Explains rapid high-dimensional near-optimality

Experiment: Isolate and evaluate all stationary points of h(t)-K32(t)
Result: Exactly five isolated stationary points, bracketed below 7e-61; largest upper value <= -1.00479e-13. Coefficient rounding remained safe.
Verdict: Strong computer-assisted evidence, not formally directed-rounded

Evidence level: Exact finite arithmetic plus analytic Gegenbauer tail
Experiment: Prove strict negativity of every unused normalized-Gegenbauer reduced cost
Result: Exact integer recurrence verifies degrees 6–14,658; a normalized-Gegenbauer tail bound proves strict negativity for every degree ≥14,659. The worst mode is r7=-2327215/9290262647272.
Verdict: Proved dual component of T30. Higher harmonic coefficients cannot improve the named auxiliary objective; primal feasibility and equality are recorded separately in T30.

Experiment: Force a degree-5 auxiliary polynomial to touch Kerdock inner products -1 and ±1/16
Result: Nonnegative Gegenbauer coefficients require parameter >= 0.00069297, while pointwise lower-bound validity requires <= -0.02387692; intervals are incompatible.
Verdict: Exact degree-5 Kerdock-contact proof impossible

Experiment: Construct nine real MUBs / 288 antipodal nodes and optimize bases, lines, non-antipodal nodes, homotopies, and twists
Result: Explicit and pair-count MSE agreed to 1.11e-16; uniform weights were optimal on support; broad searches found no better rule.
Verdict: Strong stress test, not global proof

Experiment: 10,000 random d=4 rules and 16 joint node/weight optimizations
Result: 255 random rules used negative weights; the best was at least 1.508x MUB. Joint optimizations converged to positive nearly uniform weights; best 0.0172% improvement used positive weights.
Verdict: No practical signed-weight evidence; theorem loophole remains

Experiment: Three-dimensional covariance-state propagation across widths 128–1,024
Result: Estimated finite/infinite MSE multipliers: 1.196, 1.137, 1.123, 1.078, 1.065, 1.032; width256 16-scramble mean multiplier 1.12254.
Verdict: Plausible 9–12% correction, not theorem

Experiment: 20,000-sample neuron Markov checks plus full d=4/d=16 network tests
Result: CLT-state kernel predictions improved tested individual correlations, but on 1,000 d=4 networks infinite-width and first-order predictions were excellent while CLT-state was about 4% high; d=16 was too noisy.
Verdict: Exact d=256 finite-width correction unresolved

Experiment: Independent finite-field construction of the complete dimension-256 real MUB/Kerdock rule
Result: Validated 128 alternating binary 8x8 matrices; every nonzero difference had GF(2) rank 8; 128 Hadamard bases plus the standard basis; cross-basis |inner product| exactly 1/16; 66,048 antipodal points.
Verdict: Construction independently validated

Experiment: Randomly stop after 8, 13, 32, or 64 complete Kerdock bases instead of all 129
Result: Once the 0.1 multiplier floor was reached, the score proxy was nearly flat; none beat the complete rule reliably.
Verdict: Closed; keep full rule

Experiment: Coordinate trimming, mean/median blends, early-layer deviation weighting, and standard-basis reweighting
Result: Best median blend gained below 1%; aggressive aggregation failed out of sample.
Verdict: Equal weighting remains default

Experiment: Early-layer greedy herding of Kerdock bases to match the full-design mean
Result: A 48-basis layer-1 rule looked 12.7% better in discovery but was slightly worse on holdout; score-gain estimate 0.986x with wide interval.
Verdict: Selection leakage; closed

Experiment: Choose among Kerdock rotations using exact layer-1 mean/covariance diagnostics
Result: Oracle best-of-six gap was 1.79x, but all cheap predictors had approximately zero Spearman correlation with final quality.
Verdict: Real inaccessible oracle gap; no deployable selector

Experiment: Evaluate one network-adaptively selected sign per Kerdock line
Result: Looked 10–15% better initially; final holdout score gain was 0.883x and all-32 result 0.996x before selection overhead.
Verdict: Rejected

Experiment: Blend a small structured sampler with a corrected Gaussian analytic anchor
Result: Fixed blend improved MSE from 6.17e-6 to 4.81e-6 (28.2%); target-free split-noise blend improved about 16.6%.
Verdict: Useful only for cheap/partial estimators; too costly atop full Kerdock

Experiment: Reassess 90,624-row and 78,336-row rotated-basis pilots using ensemble kernel error-cost
Result: Predicted error-cost ratios were 1.229 and 1.091; single additions, swaps, and convex reweighting did not improve.
Verdict: Rotated-pilot branch rejected

Experiment: Morton-group actual-particle thinning after layer 24 with positive reweighting to match 128 prefix features
Result: Development projected 0.873x score; strict holdout reversed to 1.069x. Weights stayed positive and well conditioned.
Verdict: Selector failed; real-particle recombination remains mechanistically informative

Experiment: Propagate full Kerdock to layer 28, retain 8,192 rows, and reweight to match anchor means
Result: Reduced compression error roughly 40–170x versus ordinary subset thinning; cost ratio 0.8983, but added MSE 1.15e-7 versus break-even 2.26e-8.
Verdict: Real effect, still 5.1x short of score break-even

Experiment: Add 64 first-tail kink-neuron activation features to anchor-mean coreset weighting
Result: Improved over mean-only weighting while retaining stable near-uniform weights, but remained far above break-even error.
Verdict: Only coreset refinement worth bounded follow-up

Experiment: Tangent/JVP grouping of nearby particles through a shared suffix linearization
Result: Produced approximately 9,000–16,000x worse error-cost.
Verdict: Catastrophic; closed

Experiment: Remaining-depth ReLU-kernel Nyström representation and thinning
Result: Suffix-kernel effective rank collapsed to about 1.001 and did not support accurate nonlinear tail compression.
Verdict: Closed in tested form

Experiment: Vector-balanced actual-particle thinning
Result: Strong single-network cancellation reversed on frozen networks.
Verdict: Failed holdout

Experiment: Extreme-enriched pilot for detecting rare final-layer switching
Result: Safe but detected too many low-impact events and spent more compute than it saved.
Verdict: Inferior; closed

Experiment: Three-tier sampled-tail estimator for stable, borderline, and switching outputs
Result: Genuinely switching outputs still required exact propagation; no score gain.
Verdict: Closed

Experiment: Low-rank final-output PCA/ridge control using exact fixed-radius mean of layer-1 activations
Result: With 2,048 fitting trajectories, gross gain 1.2302x and net gain 1.1920x; 8/8 networks improved.
Verdict: Strong synthetic candidate; official/Kerdock validation required

Experiment: Vary fitting trajectories from 512 to 4,096 and control rank/ridge
Result: Best matched net gain was 1.2329x at 2,048 trajectories; 4,096 improved gross fit but lost more production directions.
Verdict: 2,048 was best reserved-sample point in tested sweep

Experiment: Training-free expected-gate Jacobian from layer 1 to final layer with universal scale 1.25
Result: 8/8 improved; mean gross gain 1.1978x. Pilot-estimated-gate deployable version projected roughly 1.14–1.16x net.
Verdict: Robust mechanistic control, weaker than fitted low-rank control

Experiment: Four-fold antipodal-pair-preserving cross-fitting without discarding production directions
Result: Mean MSE improvement 1.244x at width 64; width-256 fold mode instability remained unresolved.
Verdict: Promising but not target-scale validated

Experiment: Add exact quadratic cross-products of dominant layer-1 covariance modes
Result: Gain changed only from about 1.206x to 1.207x.
Verdict: Negligible; closed

Experiment: Regress antipodal pair averages on centered powers |h1| through degree 4
Result: Reached only about 1.125x net.
Verdict: Inferior to basic low-rank layer-1 control

Experiment: Estimate layer-2/4/8 surrogate means with many shallow trajectories
Result: Best deeper result roughly 1.087x net versus about 1.202x for exact layer 1.
Verdict: Deeper surrogate means cost more than they save

Experiment: ReLU, tanh, and cosine shallow features with sampled feature means
Result: Best net gain only 1.029x.
Verdict: Closed

Experiment: Choose regression modes by predictable variance instead of final-output PCA
Result: Best net result about 1.135x; ordinary dominant output modes were better.
Verdict: Alternative mode objective rejected

Experiment: Combine empirical Jacobian control with a learned residual
Result: Best matched result about 1.169x net, below strongest exact-mean layer-1 control.
Verdict: Small composition gain only

Experiment: Rank-2 average true pathwise backpropagated Jacobian using 512 pilot directions
Result: Approximately 1.24x gross and 1.21x net, outperforming a larger ridge-control pilot.
Verdict: Promising derivative-enhanced control

Experiment: Frozen average-Jacobian control on independent networks
Result: About 1.25x gross and 1.23x net; 6/6 networks improved.
Verdict: Replicated on fresh synthetic networks

Experiment: Fit a small residual correction around the mechanistic pathwise-Jacobian prior
Result: With 128 pilot pairs the correction collapsed back to the prior.
Verdict: Residual not learnable at tested pilot size

Experiment: Random one-hidden-layer ReLU features on original input with analytic Gaussian means
Result: Diluted the useful layer-1 basis and reduced performance.
Verdict: Failed

Experiment: Use network-local input-gradient directions as exact-mean |u^T x| ridge features
Result: Local kink directions did not form a useful shallow dictionary.
Verdict: Failed

Experiment: Attach pathwise derivative controls at multiple intermediate depths and estimate their shallow means
Result: Deeper controls explained more variance but mean-estimation cost exceeded savings.
Verdict: Closed

Experiment: Replace pilot PCA output modes with oracle output modes
Result: Improved the control by less than 0.2%.
Verdict: Pilot PCA is not the bottleneck

Experiment: Estimate average Jacobian with scrambled Sobol-antipodal rather than random pilot directions
Result: No material improvement.
Verdict: Pilot QMC does not solve Jacobian noise

Experiment: Use the branch-selected derivative identity for q=|h1|/2 instead of averaging antipodal path gradients
Result: Best net gain increased from about 1.226x to 1.249x.
Verdict: Strongest pathwise control mechanism

Experiment: Vary pair-selected Jacobian pilot from 256 to 512 directions
Result: Optimum was flat; 256 directions preserved more production compute.
Verdict: Freeze 256-pilot setting for transfer test

Experiment: Half-normal Stein-kernel weighting of pair-selected path derivatives
Result: Small consistent improvement, raising best net gain to about 1.252x.
Verdict: Mechanistically supported incremental gain

Experiment: Replace Gaussian half-normal Stein kernel with exact fixed-radius beta-density sphere kernel
Result: Numerically indistinguishable at dimension 256.
Verdict: Confirms large-dimension mechanism; no extra gain

Experiment: Multiply Stein-weighted derivative by inverse exact covariance of absolute layer-1 features
Result: Added a small gain, reaching about 1.2525x net on tuning networks.
Verdict: Best tuned pathwise variant

Experiment: Rank-2, 256-pilot, 50% multivariate-Stein pathwise estimator with frozen settings
Result: Validated at 1.243x net with 8/8 wins on antithetic random/Sobol-style points, but a later frozen complete-Kerdock transfer test failed.
Verdict: Superseded by V59; useful on ordinary sampling but not demonstrated on full Kerdock.
Primary source: Pathwise-Stein report plus Kerdock transfer audit, 2026-07-28

Experiment: Centered powers of half-normal layer-1 magnitudes along selected derivative modes
Result: Improved only about 0.15%.
Verdict: Marginal

Experiment: Coordinatewise derivative-versus-magnitude curvature term centered analytically
Result: Raised tuned net gain to about 1.2565x.
Verdict: Small tuning improvement

Experiment: Fit full cross-coordinate gradient-versus-magnitude Jacobian and compress to rank 1–8
Result: Failed to beat the simpler diagonal term.
Verdict: Dense cross-coordinate curvature closed

Experiment: Frozen diagonal gradient-curvature correction
Result: Validated around 1.243x net with 8/8 wins, nearly identical to frozen Stein estimator.
Verdict: Optional; no demonstrated gain over simpler Stein form

Experiment: Cubic and higher centered derivative-power expansion
Result: Higher powers reduced generalization; only first curvature term survived.
Verdict: Closed beyond first curvature term

Evidence level: Width-64 discovery then full width-256 falsification
Experiment: Analytically average a fitted affine tail and sample only its nonlinear residual
Result: Width-64 suggested 1.22x; at width 256 the tail-8 hybrid was about 7x worse and tail lengths 1–4 remained negative.
Verdict: Scale-dependent false positive; closed

Experiment: Exact full-cloud final preactivation mean plus subset ReLU and linear Hermite correction
Result: At 8,192 rows, additional MSE 3.24–4.60e-8 versus break-even 5.63e-9; only 2.74% compute saved.
Verdict: Real variance reduction, 6–8x too noisy for score

Experiment: Use pilot variance/skew/kurtosis and third/fourth/sixth-order marginal corrections
Result: Best Edgeworth additional MSE 5.56e-8, worse than linear CV 3.24e-8 at every pilot size.
Verdict: Closed

Experiment: Predict tail outputs from anchor PCA plus 16–128 selected kink activations and sample a residual
Result: Best added MSE 2.03e-7 versus break-even 1.88e-8.
Verdict: Closed

Experiment: Large Kerdock surrogate stream with dead/on/kink simplification plus small exact residual stream
Result: Best projected adjusted gain 1.0632x, CI [1.0449,1.0701], 6/6 wins, but nearly all from idealized sparse arithmetic.
Verdict: Missed predeclared 1.15–1.20x gate; closed

Experiment: Linear multilevel prefix/suffix estimator
Result: Aggregate score ratio 1.248x with network range 0.62x–1.77x.
Verdict: Worse and unstable

Experiment: Nonlinear multilevel prefix/suffix estimator
Result: Aggregate score ratio 1.105x with a 4.30x outlier.
Verdict: Worse; closed

Experiment: Rank-32 final-layer low-rank control
Result: Remained about 1.31x worse.
Verdict: Catastrophic; closed

Experiment: Pilot-classify stable gates inside recursive Gaussian moment propagation
Result: Strict correction improved Gaussian rollout by only 1.9%; absolute final MSE remained about 1.3e-4.
Verdict: Stable but hundreds of times too inaccurate

Experiment: Permutation-equivariant, bounded, PSD-preserving learned closure trained through full rollout
Result: State-only model improved final MSE 3.36x at width24/depth12 and 4.29x transferring to width32/depth16.
Verdict: Strong small-regime fit

Evidence level: Depth-32 target training plus width transfer
Experiment: Fine-tune through width32/depth32 rollout and transfer to width64/depth32
Result: 10.40x improvement at training width but 0.75x at width64; oracle local moments did not fix transfer.
Verdict: Width-specific model class closed

Experiment: Feature ablation for symmetric x1 and antisymmetric x1a transported k21 slices
Result: Marginals only 0.81x; x1 1.71x; x1a 1.47x; x1+x1a 3.58x next-variance gain.
Verdict: Real localized mechanistic signal

Experiment: Small coefficient network widths 8–96 using x1/x1a
Result: 64-unit model achieved 2.20x gain at about 9.2B inference FLOPs; 96-unit 2.33x at about 20B.
Verdict: 64-unit best tested compute/accuracy compromise

Experiment: Direct full-width 10,082-parameter nonlinear coefficient model
Result: Strongest run reduced one-step variance error 3.25% to 0.856% (3.80x) on every held-out case.
Verdict: Promising one-step target-width result

Experiment: Use oracle marginals and oracle k21 features while recursively propagating off-diagonal covariance
Result: Final propagated variance error fell from 31.6% to 3.63% (8.68x), but remained inadequate.
Verdict: Shows no inherent explosion; not deployable

Experiment: Restrict learned model to ordinary finite-pilot features
Result: Learned next-variance error 3.75% versus raw sampled covariance 3.56%.
Verdict: No gain without factorized K3 x1/x1a

Experiment: Train flexible tree and compact coefficient models at smaller width and transfer with x1/x1a
Result: Tree model transferred width64→256 with 3.29x gain; compact neural coefficient model did not transfer.
Verdict: Feature law transfers in flexible model; compact runtime must train at target width

Experiment: Combine learned covariance correction with full Edgeworth mean correction
Result: Each component helped with the other held Gaussian, but full-strength combination worsened final output; damping did not robustly fix it.
Verdict: Need a mutually realizable joint state

Experiment: Rank stable-gate approximations by raw pilot tail risk
Result: Pilot ranking noise caused 8–13% misses.
Verdict: Failed

Experiment: Clustered interval bounds for stable final outputs
Result: Certified none of 151 outputs that were actually stable in the reference run.
Verdict: Axis-aligned certification ineffective

Experiment: Switch from persistent Winograd to compact dense multiplication when pilot-stable channels are dead
Result: Mean active width 222.3/256; only 0.43% of layer/network cases crossed the ~163-channel break-even; mean theoretical saving 0.011%.
Verdict: Essentially zero gain

Evidence level: Functional package tests; official execution pending
Experiment: Build IID, Sobol, Haar-10, Haar-11, Haar-12, and Haar-12-direct estimator packages and paired Mini-100 runner
Result: All packages passed contract/shape/finite-output tests; CDF approximation max error 7.45e-8. Official Mac run remains pending.
Verdict: Implementation complete; evidence unresolved

Experiment: Implement selective corpus downloader, MLP-level trainers, get_dslice((2,1)) adapters, NumPy inference, and cost models
Result: Pipeline smoke-tested end to end on schema-compatible generated files; no real-corpus training completed.
Verdict: Research infrastructure complete, not a result

Experiment: Pilot-classify nearly deterministic final outputs and exactly propagate only kink outputs with minority-tail corrections
Result: Frozen holdout score ratio 0.989754x.
Verdict: Small reproducible fallback gain

Experiment: Jointly compile stable-on/off paths in the final two layers and exactly propagate penultimate kink channels/final kink outputs
Result: MSE ratio 1.001211; effective score ratio 0.984341, bootstrap [0.979540,0.989634]; projected 1.4499e-7 from 1.4730e-7 baseline.
Verdict: Best validated fallback compiler; later modestly superseded by adaptive A19.

Experiment: Benchmark exact, pad-16, and pad-32 compiled shapes
Result: Exact score ratio 0.984341; pad-16 0.987799; pad-32 0.992829. Representative compiled layers took 0.081s versus 0.163s dense.
Verdict: Timing supports gain, but blocked-layout conversion still unmeasured

Experiment: CSR propagation for stable/kink channel subsets versus dense BLAS
Result: CSR was approximately 12x slower.
Verdict: Generic sparse matrices rejected

Evidence level: Rigorous computer-assisted proof plus clean-room regeneration
Experiment: Directed-rounding Delsarte certificate for the scoped static nonnegative class
Result: The certified statement is one-sided: actual Kerdock relative excess lies in [0, 0.02336550102949%] for the d=256, depth-32 infinite-width normalized ReLU kernel, ≤66,048 nodes, nonnegative mass-one weights, and rules independent of the realized network.
Verdict: Complete within its explicit trust base and scope. It does not prove strict suboptimality or cover finite width, arbitrary signed nodes, adaptive support/weights, or nonlinear estimators.
Primary source: T22 v5/v5.1 proof package; PROOF_AUDIT.md; canonical one-sided theorem JSON

Experiment: Split a fixed 41,280-row tail budget into 1, 2, 4, or 5 calibrated strata
Result: Projected score ratios were 0.99890, 0.99960, 1.00802, and 1.01930.
Verdict: Extra strata add calibration cost and instability; closed.

Experiment: Use disagreement between nested estimates to choose 37,152, 41,280, or 45,408 tail rows
Result: Cross-fitted projected ratio 0.99798. Independent-rotation aggregate-MSE ratio 0.99432, but uncertainty remained too large for a sub-1% claim.
Verdict: Plausible sub-percent adaptive gain; not submission-ready.

Experiment: Add predicted final preactivations, ReLU outputs, partial contributions, and layer-31 features to coreset calibration
Result: No tested feature set materially reduced compression error after its computation and calibration cost.
Verdict: Closed.

Experiment: Select tail rows using kink scores, norms, random projections, downstream proxies, leverage proxies, or quantiles
Result: Balanced random selection was best at about 0.99971 projected ratio; adaptive selectors introduced damaging outliers.
Verdict: Cheap network-specific row scoring failed; balanced random selection remains safer.

Experiment: Generate multiple balanced subsets and choose minimum prefix feature-mean discrepancy
Result: Four candidates gave about 0.99798 projected ratio on development; the planned fresh holdout was incomplete.
Verdict: Weak open lead; requires completed untouched holdout.

Experiment: Choose number of complete Kerdock bases using cheap network diagnostics
Result: Oracle mean ratio was about 0.6245, but the frozen selector averaged about 1.390 with a worst network near 6.31x.
Verdict: Large inaccessible oracle gap; closed for tested diagnostics.

Experiment: Predict the residual from 16 bases using cheap trajectory and weight statistics
Result: An apparent strong result was traced to target leakage. After removal, gain was only 1.006x and residual MSE remained 16.07x full Kerdock.
Verdict: Closed in the tested low-dimensional feature form.

Evidence level: 20 fresh width-256 networks x 4 complete-Kerdock rotations
Experiment: Apply frozen rank-2, 256-pilot, 50% multivariate-Stein control to complete Kerdock
Result: Aggregate gain 0.9369x with bootstrap interval 0.8349–1.0868, below the preregistered 1.10x continuation threshold.
Verdict: Provisionally closed on Kerdock; test used rotation variance rather than high-precision truth MSE.

Experiment: Use z=(u^T a1)^2 with analytically known expectation and downstream sensitivity direction
Result: Unamplified control reduced raw MSE 4.43%; fixed amplitude 2.209 reduced untouched-set MSE 7.33%.
Verdict: Superseded by V65: promising development result reversed on 12 genuinely fresh networks; branch closed.

Experiment: Replace the leading Jacobian singular vector with u=J·1 from one backward vector propagation
Result: Fresh-set gain 4.45%, essentially identical to the expensive singular-vector direction.
Verdict: Superseded by V65: promising development result reversed on 12 genuinely fresh networks; branch closed.

Evidence level: 32 untouched synthetic networks; two independent 262,144-point references
Family: Exact and doubled first-layer two-moment transport
Experiment: Match exact first-layer mean and second moment after the Kerdock first layer; test exact transform two1 and doubled correction two2
Result: Baseline raw MSE 3.05233e-7. two1: 2.86201e-7, 6.24% reduction, 20/32 wins, gain-ratio CI 1.018–1.113. two2: 2.75980e-7, 9.58% reduction, 20/32 wins, CI 1.007–1.209. Added arithmetic about 0.1354B operations; projected adjusted improvement about 9.54%, not official. Later cross-fitted layer-origin attribution found the causal first-layer intervention only 1.052x, with a confidence interval crossing no improvement and harmful networks.
Verdict: SUPERSEDED / STOP as a major submission path. The earlier two1/two2 synthetic average gain did not remain robust under the later attribution study; retain only as historical mechanism evidence.
Primary source: Agent 5/6 transport report and final 64-network one-pass summary, 2026-07-29

Experiment: Combine layer-1 mean transport with exact quadratic second-moment correction
Result: Raw MSE improved about 9.42%, but the tested implementation duplicated downstream trajectories.
Verdict: Statistically positive but budget-infeasible as implemented.

Experiment: Apply quadratic and layer-1 transport controls near the 10% multiplier floor
Result: Quadratic gained only 1.88%; transport worsened 4.86%; combined worsened 17.0%.
Verdict: Controls become too noisy at small point counts; closed for the floor-budget route.

Experiment: Contract learned x1/x1a covariance corrections through actual next-layer weights
Result: Validation-fitted alpha achieved 2.04x variance-MSE gain, 2.03x sigma-MSE gain, 98.3% case improvement, and sigma RMS 1.59% to 1.12%.
Verdict: Passes downstream-contraction gate; still relies on accurate/oracle transported features.

Experiment: Apply diagonal-preserving eigenvalue clipping at every recursive rollout step
Result: 435 repairs caused severe amplification; mean, variance, and sigma gains were all below 1 and only 13.3% of variance cases improved.
Verdict: Repeated PSD projection is destructive; closed.

Experiment: Predict diagonal mean-field error directly from all network weights
Result: Held-out gains were about 2.43x at width32, 1.94x at width64, and about 1.64x at width128 with cleaner labels.
Verdict: Broad analytic bias is learnable; scientifically positive but far from standalone challenge accuracy.

Evidence level: Historical held-out residual-learning report; decisive rows incomplete in archive
Experiment: Predict Kerdock error vector or multiplicative scale from network weights
Result: The archived qualitative conclusion is that tested weight-space representations did not recover stable signed network-specific Kerdock residuals. The previously quoted 0.94–0.99x numerical range lacks the decisive row package and should not be used as a paper number.
Verdict: Retain as qualitative historical evidence only; do not treat as universal unlearnability or cite exact ratios until the original rows, splits, metric code, and hashes are restored.
Primary source: Historical weight-space report; Agent9 evidence audit

Experiment: Fit one oracle multiplicative scalar per network in Y≈(1+c)K
Result: Oracle scalar correction improved 17.68x at width32 and 3.82x at width64; most width32 error lay in this mode.
Verdict: Residual is simple within a network but unpredictable from tested observables.

Experiment: Shrink only the leading covariance eigenvalue in early layers, fading from 0.8 to 1 by layer 16
Result: Holdout analytic-estimator MSE improved to about 2.60e-5; broader shrinkage variants failed.
Verdict: Specific finite-width mechanism identified, but absolute error remains far above Kerdock.

Experiment: Select suffix depth 2–6 from pilot kink counts and compile stable-on/off paths
Result: Raw-MSE ratio 1.00170; ideal arithmetic ratio 0.95358; calibrated effective-score ratio 0.97865 [0.97566,0.98163], with 59/60 calibrated wins. Projected score about 1.442e-7.
Verdict: Strongest new honest near-term candidate; integrate and grade.

Experiment: Extend candidate maximum depth from 6 to 7–8
Result: Depth 7 was selected once and depth 8 never; gain was negligible while symbolic complexity grew.
Verdict: Stop at maximum depth 6.

Experiment: Test minority threshold 2, half-size pilots, and alternative pilot geometries
Result: Threshold 2 was marginal and post-selected; smaller pilots increased missed-switch error; alternate geometries gave no robust gain.
Verdict: Freeze threshold 1 and the existing 2,064-row balanced pilot.

Experiment: Run raw-BLAS 90,624-row multifidelity estimator through local and subprocess runners
Result: Local mode misleadingly recorded zero FLOPs. Subprocess mode enforced immutable FlopScope arrays; honest functional execution would charge roughly 373B FLOPs, above budget.
Verdict: Scoring/accounting workaround invalid; do not pursue.
Primary source: Official subprocess logs and accounting audit, 2026-07-28

Experiment: Compute exact degree-1 and degree-2 first-layer Hermite controls with analytically known Gaussian expectation
Result: After exact radial integration the control is an angular polynomial of degree <=2. Complete Kerdock is exact through degree 5, so E[g]-Q_K(g)=0 exactly; linear downstream propagation does not change this.
Verdict: Analytic no-op; STOP before implementation or holdout use.

Evidence level: Finite-population identity plus prior 32-network transport artifacts
Experiment: Apply aggressive first-layer moment transport to all Kerdock rows, then estimate its bias from an untouched uniform subset of row differences
Result: The subset correction restores the original Kerdock row mean in expectation and adds finite-population sampling variance. It therefore removes the transport gain rather than debiasing toward Gaussian truth.
Verdict: STOP subset debiasing. Continue only undebiased two1/two2 transport for official validation.

Evidence level: Analytic identity for arbitrary learned coefficients
Experiment: Train a permutation-equivariant weight encoder that outputs multivariate Hermite coefficients of degrees 1–4
Result: Correct radialization leaves an angular polynomial of degree <=4, which Kerdock integrates exactly. The learned coefficients cannot create a nonzero correction in exact arithmetic.
Verdict: Analytic no-op; STOP before training.

Evidence level: Closest completed screens and cost lower bound
Experiment: Use 4–16 learned projections with one-dimensional nonpolynomial ridge functions and exact Gaussian integrals
Result: Closest nonlinear controls achieved only about 1.029x net; degree<=4 pair controls about 1.125x; complete-Kerdock pathwise transfer was 0.9369x. Inference lower bound is about 0.271B–1.082B FLOPs before the encoder.
Verdict: Below the 1.3x major-path gate; STOP full training. Reopen only for a preregistered degree>=6 oracle screen.

Evidence level: Analytic blockwise identity plus prior Kerdock-transfer evidence
Experiment: Use polynomial Stein fields through degree 4 or one-hidden-layer bias-free ReLU Stein components, including separate positive and negative components
Result: Polynomial fields are integrated exactly by Kerdock. Every tested one-hidden-layer bias-free ReLU Stein component averaged to zero on each individual basis block; maximum numerical block residual was 3.12e-17. A meaningful depth-2 rank-2 8x8 field would add about 0.839B FLOPs, while prior full-Kerdock transfer was negative.
Verdict: STOP current Stein/signed-neural family on complete Kerdock.

Experiment: Fit signed weights on the 129 Kerdock basis-block means while preserving exactness through degree 5, including cross-fit and residual variants
Result: The degree-4 basis-block moment tensors have a full-rank Gram matrix. Total weight one plus degree<=5 exactness uniquely forces all 129 weights to 1/129. Half-fold rules cannot satisfy the constraints; recombination reduces to uniform Kerdock.
Verdict: Analytically closed unless the degree<=5 guarantee is explicitly abandoned.

Evidence level: Software tests plus full-width integration smoke
